A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Repo2Run, with matching architecture, principal experiments and repository-level results despite retitling and reorganization. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 420 repositories, component ablations, runtime and action-use analyses, and an eight-developer manual study.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds a rollback-specific ablation, Dockerfile-quality evaluation, failure analyses and evaluation on 59 industry-grade repositories.

M1.justification: The dual environments, snapshot rollback, dependency management, test-file restrictions and Dockerfile conversion procedure are retained. The build/record phases and renamed Dockerfile synthesizer reorganize the existing method; the appendix tool definitions and safe-command list also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a separately selected evaluation of 59 popular industry-grade repositories with tests and at least 10,000 lines of code, including Flask, pandas and requests. This materially extends the represented repository population beyond the original 2024-created benchmark. The original 420-repository coverage and developer study are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain pipreqs, the README-based LLM generator and SWE-agent. The new Dockerfile-quality comparison uses the same comparator set. Appendix H.2 discloses SWE-agent settings without establishing a change to the previously evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces hadolint warning counts for evaluating successfully generated Dockerfiles and popularity/test/LOC selection criteria for the industry-grade evaluation. The original benchmark protocol, GPT-4o model and temperature remain unchanged. Renaming ECSR to EBSR does not change its definition.

E4.justification: v3 adds an isolated rollback ablation, domain and repository-size breakdowns, categorization of all 59 benchmark failures, Dockerfile-quality analysis and 30 package-installation pollution examples. These substantially expand investigation of mechanism effectiveness and failure conditions. The existing action-use analysis and deepfolio case are relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated benchmark runs, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained runtime and action-frequency reporting is unchanged; the new descriptive counts and LOC summaries do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 and all 420 appendix commit/status entries are unchanged. New results include 407 buildable Dockerfiles and 351 successful environments without rollback, 30 successes among 59 industry-grade repositories, and hadolint warning values of 5.42 versus 10.16 for Repo2Run versus the LLM generator. These are additional evaluations, not changes to the original 86.0% success rate.

T1.justification: v1's explicit agent-policy and rollback function definitions, including Equations 4 and 7, are omitted in v3 and replaced by operational prose. The basic state-transition, base-image and verification formulation remains equivalent. This is a limited reduction in formalization; neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 adds explicit positioning of Repo2Run as infrastructure for scaling executable code data and environments for coding-agent research. Its abstract foregrounds the SWE-agent comparison using the existing results. The first-agent claim, Python focus in the body and conclusion, and 86.0% benchmark success claim remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds arguments that the benchmark's domain distribution represents real-world Python repositories, interprets failures as external constraints versus timeouts, and treats fewer hadolint warnings as evidence of Dockerfile quality. The manual-time comparison and explanation of the deepfolio failure remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies project-resource and manual-study-log links and the full SWE-agent prompt/configuration in Appendix H.2, including window, overlap and history settings. v1 only states that SWE-agent prompts were adjusted. These improve documentation without establishing that existing experiments were rerun or their settings changed.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially recast around executable environments for training coding agents, with new discussion of SWE-Fixer, SWE-RL, SWE-Gym and SWE-Smith and an explicit ReAct connection. v1's R2E citation is removed. The existing Dockerfile-generation and general-agent literature reviews are largely retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The method gains a separate Dockerfile-synthesizer subsection and build/record narrative, while detailed examples, action-use discussion and the failure case move into reorganized appendices. Terminology changes broadly from configuration to building, and the separate Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: v3 adds introductory pipeline and SWE-agent-failure illustrations, simplified workflow and synthesis-rule diagrams, and several analysis tables. Main result tables separate counts from percentages and display ablation drops. Existing detailed workflow, synthesis example, action-frequency plot and failure illustration are relocated, with substantial accompanying layout changes.

improvement.justification: The isolated rollback ablation improves attribution beyond v1's broad component ablations, while industrial validation and disclosed baseline settings add useful evidence and transparency. The gain is limited by reporting defects in the new material: Table 11 labels 40 of 59 repositories as 9.3%, and its corresponding subgroup counts sum to 38. These inconsistencies weaken the added industrial summary, although the central results remain intact.
